audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL topics (JSON-RPC state queries via EIP-1898, EVM gas metering, KECCAK256 opcode, EVM tracing) and CL topics (Bellatrix P2P gossip/req-resp, Fulu fork choice with column-based DAS, network upgrade scheduling). P2P protocol changes (eth/69 EIP-7642, eth/70 EIP-7542) span both layers.

in_scope: P2P Protocol (eth/69, eth/70) handshake and data exchange
Gas Economics (memory, storage, blob, call mechanics)

el_attack_vectors.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (eth_getBalance, eth_getStorageAt, eth_call with EIP-1898 block params)
el_attack_vectors.threat: Submit malformed block parameters (both blockNumber and blockHash), attempt to query non-canonical state to mislead DApps, resource exhaustion via repeated state queries for pruned blocks
False block range advertisements to disrupt sync, Sybil attacks with coordinated false range claims, dishonest history range reports, eclipse attacks via peer slot manipulation

el_attack_vectors.entry_point: EVM Execution (KECCAK256 opcode with large memory params)
el_attack_vectors.threat: Memory exhaustion via large KECCAK256 inputs, gas-related attacks exploiting word-count rounding, attempt to exploit memory expansion cost calculations

cl_attack_vectors.threat: Propose blocks with invalid execution payloads that pass consensus checks but fail execution validation, exploiting the no-downscore policy for execution-only invalidity to flood network with 10MiB blocks
Selective column withholding to prevent DAS verification, forge column sidecars with invalid KZG proofs, delay data availability to stall fork choice
Provide incorrect checkpoint data, denial of service against data availability

misclassified_entities.reason: Ethereum Core Developers (EIP-1872) are a governance/process entity, not a runtime external entity interacting with the system at execution time. Upgrade scheduling is an offline process.
Client Development Teams (EIP-1872) are an offline development entity. They implement upgrades but do not interact with the running system as external data sources.
Node Operators (EIP-1872) manage infrastructure but are not runtime external entities sending data into the system boundary. Their interaction is operational (updating software), not protocol-level.

Debugging/Analysis Tool (EVM Trace) is a local operator tool, not an external entity crossing a trust boundary at the protocol level. It runs within the node operator's trust domain and requires local access.
Coordinated Malicious Peers (EIP-7542) is an attack scenario description, not a distinct entity class. These are covered by the general EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P entity with UNTRUSTED trust level.

trusted_external_entities.name: User/DApp via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (eth_getBalance, eth_getStorageAt, eth_call, eth_getCode with EIP-1898 block parameters)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: JSON-RPC is a public, unauthenticated interface. Clients can submit arbitrary block parameters including malformed objects (both blockNumber and blockHash present), non-existent block hashes, or references to non-canonical blocks. All parameter formats must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via eth/69 Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Peers may advertise false history ranges (earliestBlock/latestBlock), send malformed status messages, or provide corrupted receipts without bloom filters. Range claims are unverified until blocks are actually requested.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via eth/70 Protocol
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth/70 Status handshake with blockRange, RequestBlockRange (0x0b), SendBlockRange (0x0c)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Peers may advertise false block ranges to attract connections, waste bandwidth via Sybil attacks with coordinated false advertisements, or fail to serve blocks within claimed ranges. The protocol has no built-in verification of range claims.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via CL Gossip (Bellatrix+)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL gossip peers are unauthenticated at the network level. Peers may send blocks with invalid execution payloads (up to 10 MiB each) that pass consensus validation but fail execution checks. The Bellatrix spec explicitly warns against downscoring peers for execution-only invalidity, creating a potential DoS vector.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peers (Column Sidecar Sources)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P column sidecar gossip and req-resp (Fulu DAS)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Column sidecar providers are unauthenticated P2P peers. They may withhold specific columns to prevent data availability verification, provide sidecars with invalid KZG proofs, or delay responses beyond MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS. All sidecars must be structurally verified and KZG-proof-checked.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer via P2P Network (Fulu)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Signed beacon block via P2P gossip for fork choice processing
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers submit signed beacon blocks for fork choice processing. A malicious proposer may submit blocks with unavailable data (columns not published), triggering the queuing mechanism. Blocks must pass parent validation, slot validation, finality checks, and DAS-based data availability before acceptance.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: JSON-RPC state query methods (eth_getBalance, eth_getStorageAt, eth_call, eth_getCode)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block parameter must be validated: detect format (hex string, tag, or object), validate mutual exclusivity of blockNumber/blockHash in object format, verify block existence (error -32001 if not found), check canonical status if requireCanonical=true (error -32000 if non-canonical). Historical state must be available for the requested block.

Object-format parameters must not contain both blockNumber and blockHash simultaneously. Parameter type detection must handle all three formats (hex, tag, object) without ambiguity. Invalid formats must return appropriate JSON-RPC errors.

Peer status must be validated: networkid, genesis hash, and forkid must match. Incompatible peers must be disconnected. The earliestBlock and latestBlock values are self-reported and cannot be trusted until verified by actual block requests.

Block range updates are rate-limited (max once per epoch/32 blocks). Range claims must be treated as unverified. Peers failing to serve blocks within claimed ranges should be penalized via peer scoring. No more than one update per epoch should be accepted.

Receipts in eth/69 format omit bloom filters. Receiving nodes must recompute bloom filters from logs if needed for local queries. Receipt data must be validated against expected block hashes. The compact format [tx-type, post-state-or-status, cumulative-gas, logs] must be correctly parsed.

Status message validation: networkid, genesis, forkid must match. blockRange is self-reported and unverified. Peer's claimed range must be stored but not trusted until validated by actual block requests.

Range responses may contain multiple [startBlock, endBlock] tuples representing non-contiguous ranges. Responses must be treated as unverified claims. Dishonest range claims detected via failed block requests should trigger peer scoring penalties. Sybil resistance depends on diverse peer selection.

Blocks must pass consensus-layer validation (slot, proposer, signature, parent) and execution payload timestamp check before propagation. Blocks with invalid execution payloads SHOULD NOT cause peer downscoring (prevents network segregation between optimistic and non-optimistic nodes). Message size up to 10 MiB due to ExecutionPayload.
Responses must use correct fork-version-appropriate SSZ schema (phase0, altair, or bellatrix) for each requested block. Response chunks limited to 10 MiB each. Fork version determined by block slot.

All column sidecars must be structurally verified via verify_data_column_sidecar and cryptographically verified via verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs. Retrieval failure triggers block queuing (not rejection). Data availability is guaranteed only within MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS window.

Blocks must pass sequential validation: parent exists in store, slot is valid, finality constraints met, data availability confirmed via DAS (is_data_available without blob_kzg_commitments). Only after all checks pass is state transition executed. Blocks failing DA check MAY be queued for later processing.

notes: EIP-7568 (network upgrade reference) has no external entities — it is a documentation/reference EIP with no runtime protocol interactions.
Prague KECCAK256 and Gas metering subgraphs have no external entities — they model internal EVM execution mechanics with no external trust boundaries.
EVM Trace debugging tool (EXT-DEBUGGING-TOOL) was reclassified as internal — it operates within the node operator's trust domain.
EIP-1872 entities (EXT-CORE-DEVS, EXT-CLIENT-TEAMS, EXT-NETWORK-OPERATORS) were reclassified as governance/process entities, not runtime protocol entities.
EXT-MALICIOUS-PEERS from EIP-7542 was reclassified as an attack scenario covered by the general peer entity.
